sentences.en: We're currently just two days away from the start of the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris.
sentences.zh: 距离2024年巴黎夏季奥运会开幕还有两天。

sentences.en: And if you couldn't already tell from the TV commercials, the branded soda cans, and the Emily in Paris SpawnCon,
sentences.zh: 如果你们还没从电视广告、品牌汽水罐以及《艾米丽在巴黎》的各种联动中看出来的话，

sentences.en: the Olympics are, once again, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 奥运会再次席卷了全球。

sentences.en: So in the Olympic spirit, we are bringing you four stories about the Games in all their international theatrical glory.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了响应奥运精神，我们将为大家带来四个关于奥运会的故事，展现其国际盛会的辉煌与戏剧性。

sentences.en: Starting with one from 99% Invisible Supervising producer, Christopher Johnson.
sentences.zh: 首先由《99%隐形》的监制克里斯托弗·约翰逊带来第一个故事。
你好，克里斯托弗·约翰逊。

sentences.en: What do you have for me today?
sentences.zh: 今天你给我带来了什么？

sentences.en: So this summer, for the first time ever, there'll be Olympic-level breakdancing.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，奥运会将首次迎来奥运级别的霹雳舞比赛。

sentences.en: It's officially called breaking, and it's the first ever so-called dance sport to happen in Summer Olympics history.
sentences.zh: 它正式名称叫“Breaking”，这是夏季奥运会历史上首次出现的所谓舞蹈类运动项目。

sentences.en: Wow, I did not know that.
I support all things breakdancing, especially because I'm a hip-hop head.
sentences.zh: 我支持所有关于霹雳舞的事物，尤其是因为我本人就是个嘻哈迷。

sentences.en: But breaking is not like running or swimming or throwing stuff.
sentences.zh: 但霹雳舞不像跑步、游泳或投掷类项目那样。

sentences.en: It's not your typical Olympic sport.
sentences.zh: 它不是那种典型的奥运项目。

sentences.en: And this got me thinking, as unusual as Olympic breakdancing might seem,
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁思考，尽管奥运霹雳舞看起来可能有些不同寻常，

sentences.en: it cannot be the oddest event to ever be in the Games.
sentences.zh: 但它绝不可能是奥运史上最奇葩的项目。

sentences.en: Okay, so first of all, I need you to know that many of the weirdest Olympic sports in history
sentences.zh: 好的，首先你需要知道，历史上许多最奇怪的奥运项目，

sentences.en: came into being way back before the Olympics were considered the pinnacle of professional athletics.
sentences.zh: 都是在奥运会被视为职业竞技巅峰之前出现的。

sentences.en: Those earliest Games were actually meant for amateurs.
sentences.zh: 最初的奥运会其实是为业余选手准备的。

sentences.en: The modern Games were started in 1896 by this French aristocrat named Pierre de Coubertin.
sentences.zh: 现代奥运会是由一位名叫皮埃尔·德·顾拜旦的法国贵族于1896年发起的。

sentences.en: This guy's life is a whole story in itself.
sentences.zh: 这家伙的一生本身就是一个传奇故事。

sentences.en: But basically, the Olympics were his dream.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，奥运会是他的梦想。

sentences.en: He pitched it in lectures all over France, like,
sentences.zh: 他在法国各地发表演讲，推销他的理念，比如：

sentences.en: let's all get together and play sports and then hand out medals and trophies.
sentences.zh: 让我们聚在一起进行体育比赛，然后颁发奖牌和奖杯。

sentences.en: And these sports were definitely not for professional athletes.
sentences.zh: 而且这些运动绝对不是为职业运动员准备的。

sentences.en: These were for, like, average amateurs.
sentences.zh: 它们是为普通业余爱好者准备的。

sentences.en: And when the Olympics began, the spirit of the Games was hardcore amateurism.
sentences.zh: 当奥运会开始时，其精神核心就是纯粹的业余主义。

sentences.en: So at that point, the one-offs and the crazies and all sorts of folks just show up.
sentences.zh: 所以在那时，各种稀奇古怪的人和项目都会冒出来。

sentences.en: I talked to David Goldblatt, who wrote a book called The Games,
sentences.zh: 我采访了戴维·戈德布拉特，他写过一本名为《奥运会：全球史》的书，

sentences.en: A Global History of the Olympics, and he told me just how casual the earliest Olympic Games were.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我早期的奥运会是多么随意。

sentences.en: I mean, in 1896, at the Athens Games, the first Games,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在1896年雅典奥运会，也就是第一届奥运会上，

sentences.en: the guys that won the pistol competition are two brothers from Harvard, and they're on holiday.
sentences.zh: 赢得手枪射击比赛的人是来自哈佛大学的两兄弟，他们当时正在度假。

sentences.en: So these guys just rolled up to the Olympics pistol event, like,
sentences.zh: 所以这些人就直接跑去参加奥运会的手枪比赛，就像是说：

sentences.en: hey, y'all, we have guns, we can shoot.
sentences.zh: 嘿，各位，我们有枪，我们能射击。
他们就这么直接出现了。

sentences.en: They had their pistols with them, of course, you know, as everybody does when they travel.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们随身带着手枪，你知道的，就像每个人旅行时都会带的那样。

sentences.en: So in the first modern Olympics, people could just, like, walk on off the street and they could participate.
sentences.zh: 所以第一届现代奥运会，人们真的可以从街上走过来直接参赛。

sentences.en: And the fact that the Olympics were new and experimental and not at all about being a pro,
sentences.zh: 事实上，奥运会当时是全新的、实验性的，完全不讲究职业化，

sentences.en: that opened the door to all sorts of sports being in those early Games.
sentences.zh: 这为各种各样的运动进入早期奥运会打开了大门。

sentences.en: For example, in the second ever modern Olympic Games, one of the events was firefighting.
sentences.zh: 例如，在第二届现代奥运会上，其中一个项目竟然是消防演习。

sentences.en: So they lit a house on fire and you had to put that out and then you had to do a fake rescue.
sentences.zh: 他们会点燃一栋房子，你必须把它扑灭，然后还要进行一场模拟救援。

sentences.en: The 1900 Games also had this aquatics event where you'd go under boats and then over boats and then under some more boats.
sentences.zh: 1900年奥运会还有一个水上项目，你需要从船下穿过，再从船上翻过，然后再穿过更多船只。
这真是一个了不起的项目。

sentences.en: And you had swimmers diving off boats that had been moored on the river.
sentences.zh: 选手们从停泊在河上的船只上跳入水中。

sentences.en: And they would swim, you know, 20 meters.
sentences.zh: 然后他们要游，你知道的，20米。

sentences.en: And then they would have to either go under a second set of boats and come out the other side.
sentences.zh: 接着他们必须从第二组船只下方游过，并从另一侧出来。

sentences.en: Or sometimes they had to clamber into the boat and then dive off back into the river.
sentences.zh: 或者有时他们必须爬进船里，然后再跳回河里。

sentences.en: And this is all happening on the seine.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在塞纳河上。

sentences.en: Lord knows what the condition of the water was.
sentences.zh: 天知道当时的水质状况如何。

sentences.en: Other events from the 1900 Games include hot air balloon racing and croquet and cannon shooting.
sentences.zh: 1900年奥运会的其他项目还包括热气球比赛、槌球和火炮射击。

sentences.en: Can you imagine cannon shooting in the Olympics?
sentences.zh: 你能想象奥运会上还有火炮射击吗？

sentences.en: So if I'm hearing you right, the 1900 Games specifically was the one with so many great unusual events.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我没听错的话，1900年奥运会就是那个拥有许多奇葩项目的奥运会。

sentences.en: One reason these Olympics have so many random events may very well be because the 1900 Games weren't really actually, factually, officially recognized as the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 这些奥运会有这么多随机项目的一个原因，很可能是因为1900年奥运会实际上并没有被官方正式承认为奥运会。

sentences.en: At least not until like 80 years later.
So what do you mean by that?
So in 1900, the Olympics was just in its second year.
sentences.zh: 1900年时，奥运会才举办到第二届。

sentences.en: And it wasn't its own established standalone thing yet.
sentences.zh: 它还没有成为一个独立的、成熟的赛事。

sentences.en: So they kind of just glommed on to the World's Fair, which was also happening in Paris at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是附着在当时同样在巴黎举办的世界博览会上。

sentences.en: And the World's Fair people really didn't know what the hell the Olympics even were.
sentences.zh: 而世博会的人根本不知道奥运会到底是什么鬼东西。

sentences.en: Some folks thought it was this weird neo-Hellenic cult.
sentences.zh: 有些人以为这是一种奇怪的新希腊邪教。

sentences.en: Nobody really knew that the Olympics were going on.
sentences.zh: 没人真正知道奥运会正在进行中。

sentences.en: There were no posters with Olympic insignia around.
sentences.zh: 周围没有任何带有奥运标志的海报。

sentences.en: The press referred to it as the international games or, you know, they didn't quite know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 媒体称之为“国际运动会”，或者说，他们根本不知道该怎么处理它。

sentences.en: The 1900 Games were also an outlier in much of Olympic history because instead of lasting just two weeks, those games lasted five whole months.
sentences.zh: 1900年奥运会也是奥运史上的一大异类，因为那届奥运会持续了整整五个月，而不是两周。

sentences.en: And they had more than double the events that we have today.
sentences.zh: 而且它的项目数量是今天的两倍多。

sentences.en: And in the end, the IOC had to go back 80 years later and decide which of those weirdo events were even going to count in the Olympic records.
sentences.zh: 最终，国际奥委会不得不在80年后回过头来，决定哪些奇葩项目能计入奥运纪录。

sentences.en: It was only in the 1980s that actually a definitive list of who won what, what events were Olympic and which weren't, were drawn up by the IOC.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪80年代，国际奥委会才制定了一份确定的名单，明确谁赢了什么，哪些项目是奥运项目，哪些不是。

sentences.en: And one event that most definitely was not considered Olympic was the firefighters.
sentences.zh: 而最肯定不被视为奥运项目的一个就是消防演习。

sentences.en: Rest in peace, firefighting in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 安息吧，奥运会消防演习。

sentences.en: But listen, listen, the fun Olympic sports didn't end with 1900.
sentences.zh: 但听着，听着，有趣的奥运项目并没有在1900年结束。

sentences.en: And in fact, one of those sports put the United States at the center of an Olympic scandal.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一项运动让美国陷入了一场奥运丑闻。

sentences.en: And that sport was tug of war.
Tug of war is an absolutely fantastic sport.
sentences.zh: 拔河是一项绝对精彩的运动。

sentences.en: I can't believe, actually, that we don't still have it in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 我真不敢相信我们现在竟然没有把它保留在奥运会里。

sentences.en: So you might think of tug of war as something you did as part of field day when you were growing up,
sentences.zh: 你可能觉得拔河是你小时候运动会的一部分，

sentences.en: like right after the sack races and before running with an egg on a spoon.
sentences.zh: 就像在麻袋赛跑之后，勺子运蛋跑之前的那种活动。

sentences.en: But in the early 1900s, tug of war, Roman Mars, was hot.
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪初，罗曼·马尔斯，拔河可是非常火的。

sentences.en: So hot, it was in five summer games.
sentences.zh: 火到它出现在了五届夏季奥运会上。

sentences.en: I mean, this is also, strikes me, is super fun to watch.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在我看来，看起来超级有趣。

sentences.en: You get all these like gigantic Andre the Giant, like with the singlet on, you're like WrestleMania 3 style, you know, like.
sentences.zh: 你会看到像安德烈巨人那样巨大的家伙，穿着紧身衣，就像《摔角狂热3》那种风格，你知道的。

sentences.en: And just like pulling on things, you just get your biggest dudes in the whole country.
sentences.zh: 大家都在用力拉，你只需要找来全国最强壮的家伙。

sentences.en: It is everything that you're picturing.
sentences.zh: 这和你想象的一模一样。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, between five and eight guys, the numbers changed over time.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你知道的，每边五到八个人，人数随时间而变。

sentences.en: On each side, pulling for their lives.
sentences.zh: 在每一边，为了生存而拼命拉扯。

sentences.en: But for such a simple sport, Olympic tug of war got a little spicy, Roman.
sentences.zh: 但对于这样一项简单的运动，奥运拔河变得有点火药味了，罗曼。

sentences.en: Lots of little scandals along the way.
The 1908 games in London are probably the best example of that.
sentences.zh: 1908年伦敦奥运会可能是最好的例子。

sentences.en: You've got a British team and an American team contesting.
sentences.zh: 当时有英国队和美国队在竞争。

sentences.en: The Americans, it's basically a scratch team.
sentences.zh: 美国队基本上是一支临时拼凑的队伍。

sentences.en: It's like the wrestlers and the heavy guys from the field events, and they're put together.
sentences.zh: 就像是摔跤手和那些田径项目的大块头被凑在一起。

sentences.en: And they're going against the Brits, who have a legit tug of war team.
sentences.zh: 他们要对抗英国队，那可是正儿八经的拔河队。

sentences.en: They're all members of the Liverpool City Police, and they're hella strong.
sentences.zh: 他们全是利物浦市警察局的成员，强得离谱。

sentences.en: Tug of war is what they do.
sentences.zh: 拔河就是他们的本职工作。

sentences.en: But the real edge that the Brits have got is that these guys show up in their work boots,
sentences.zh: 但英国队真正的优势在于，这些人穿着工作靴上场，

sentences.en: And you can imagine, given how tug of war works,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，考虑到拔河的原理，

sentences.en: that is giving you a real edge over a bunch of guys who are wearing their track shoes.
sentences.zh: 这比那些穿着普通运动鞋的家伙确实有很大优势。

sentences.en: The Liverpool team absolutely crushed them.
sentences.zh: 利物浦队彻底碾压了他们。

sentences.en: The Americans, of course, incensed, saying this can't possibly be in the rules.
sentences.zh: 美国人当然很愤怒，说这绝对不符合规则。

sentences.en: And the Americans apparently left in a huff.
sentences.zh: 而美国人显然气冲冲地离开了。

sentences.en: What I love about this moment is that the American sports press,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个时刻的原因是，当时的美国体育媒体，

sentences.en: which is just kind of finding its hyperbolic voice at this moment in history,
sentences.zh: 正处于历史中夸张修辞风格的萌芽期，
他们对这次事件进行了报道。

sentences.en: And the New York Evening Post said of the City of Liverpool police boots,
sentences.zh: 《纽约晚邮报》在谈到利物浦市警察的靴子时说，

sentences.en: they had inch-thick soles and were heavier than those worn in the English Navy,
sentences.zh: 它们的鞋底有一英寸厚，比英国海军穿的还要重，

sentences.en: while the New York Evening World thought the boots were as big as North River ferry boats.
sentences.zh: 而《纽约晚报》则认为那些靴子大得像北河的渡轮。

sentences.en: By the way, at that same Olympics, another British tug-of-war team,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，在同一届奥运会上，另一支英国拔河队，

sentences.en: the City of London police team,
they later challenged the Americans to a match in just their socks.
sentences.zh: 他们后来挑战美国队，要求只穿袜子进行比赛。

sentences.en: And the Americans said, no thanks.
sentences.zh: 而美国人说，不用了，谢谢。

sentences.en: Okay, so they probably knew what was up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他们大概知道是怎么回事了。

sentences.en: You see how it is there.
sentences.zh: 你明白那里的情况了吧。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, sadly, we no longer have Olympic-level tug-of-war.
sentences.zh: 现在，显然，可悲的是，我们不再有奥运级别的拔河比赛了。
再次重申，这真是犯罪般的遗憾。

sentences.en: We also don't have obstacle swimming or cannon shooting.
sentences.zh: 我们也没有障碍游泳或大炮射击比赛。

sentences.en: Most of them disappeared pretty quickly once the Olympics became the professionalized event
sentences.zh: 一旦奥运会演变成我们今天所熟知的职业化赛事，它们中的大多数很快就消失了。

sentences.en: that we know it to be today.
But that doesn't mean that we lost all interesting sports,
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我们失去了所有有趣的运动，

sentences.en: because there's a whole other category known as demonstration sports.
sentences.zh: 因为还有另一大类被称为表演项目。

sentences.en: I think I have some idea what those are, but could you describe demonstration sports to me?
sentences.zh: 我想我大概知道那是什么，但你能给我介绍一下表演项目吗？

sentences.en: So those are essentially sports from specific regions in the world
sentences.zh: 它们本质上是来自世界特定地区的运动，

sentences.en: that aren't meant to be official sports just yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还不是正式的比赛项目。

sentences.en: They're kind of just played for show and to promote the international spirit of the games.
sentences.zh: 它们主要是为了展示，并促进奥运会的国际精神。

sentences.en: And usually it's an opportunity to showcase a sport that is not globally particularly well-known,
sentences.zh: 通常这是一个展示那些在全球范围内不太知名，

sentences.en: but which, you know, is important to that nation.
sentences.zh: 但对该国很重要的运动的机会。

sentences.en: So, for example, there's this sport called glima, which is basically Viking wrestling.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一种叫“格里马”（glima）的运动，基本上就是维京摔跤。

sentences.en: That was a demo sport in 1912.
Later, you get Swedish gymnastics, which I didn't know existed.
sentences.zh: 后来还有瑞典体操，我以前都不知道它的存在。

sentences.en: There's korfball, which shined for a couple of years in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 还有荷兰式篮球（korfball），它在20世纪20年代曾风靡过几年。

sentences.en: But some events do eventually become permanent fixtures of the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 但有些项目最终确实成为了奥运会的常设项目。

sentences.en: So, in 1964, for example, judo became a demonstration sport.
sentences.zh: 例如，1964年，柔道成为了表演项目。

sentences.en: And in the case of judo, and this is also true of taekwondo,
sentences.zh: 以柔道为例，跆拳道也是如此，

sentences.en: first introduced as a demonstration sport by the South Koreans at the 1988 Seoul Olympics,
sentences.zh: 它们最初由韩国人在1988年汉城奥运会上作为表演项目引入，

sentences.en: they then go on to be permanent Olympic sports.
sentences.zh: 随后便成为了永久的奥运比赛项目。

sentences.en: I mean, that is nice that they can introduce new things
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们能引入新事物，

sentences.en: and then have them be adopted as more and more of the world takes them on
sentences.zh: 并随着世界上越来越多的人接受它们，
使它们不再仅仅是区域性运动，这确实很好。

sentences.en: I mean, do we have any cool demo sports this year that you're aware of?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知不知道今年有什么酷的表演项目？

sentences.en: The last demo games included in the Olympics were actually way back in 1992,
sentences.zh: 奥运会上最后一次包含表演项目实际上要追溯到1992年，

sentences.en: which had several games, including roller hockey.
sentences.zh: 当时有几个项目，包括轮滑曲棍球。

sentences.en: Well, if we don't get any demo sports, at least we have breaking to look forward to.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果没有表演项目，至少我们还有霹雳舞可以期待。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for this, Christopher.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你，克里斯托弗。

sentences.en: When a city hosts the Olympics,
sentences.zh: 当一个城市举办奥运会时，

sentences.en: they have to construct a ton of new buildings,
sentences.zh: 他们必须建造大量的新建筑，

sentences.en: like an entire village to house the athletes,
and a track and field stadium,
and a specialty venue for bicycle races,
sentences.zh: 以及专门的自行车赛场，

sentences.en: and the list can get very long.
Sometimes those structures end up being a fixture of civic life for years to come,
sentences.zh: 有时这些建筑最终会成为未来多年的城市生活设施，

sentences.en: like the London Stadium, which now hosts soccer games,
sentences.zh: 比如伦敦体育场，现在举办足球比赛，
或者亚特兰大运动员村，

sentences.en: which has been converted into student housing.
sentences.zh: 它已经被改造成了学生公寓。

sentences.en: But there are also venues that become white elephants,
